links.outcome: Accuracy of clinical calculator results from direct model arithmetic versus solver hand-off
links.effect: Direct model arithmetic reached 72.02% (7B) and 83.47% (32B); solver hand-off gave 75.31% (7B, not reliably better) and 90.53% (32B, +7.05 points).
links.quote: With formulas and gold variables supplied and both routes reading the whole note, handing off to the solver is not a reliable advantage at 7B (75.31% against 72.02%, a paired +3.29 points with a 95% calculator-cluster interval of [-3.49, 10.38]) but is one at 32B (90.53% against 83.47%, +7.05 [0.47, 14.60], clear of zero).

unlisted_practices: Having the LLM write case-specific code that a restricted deterministic executor runs instead of doing arithmetic itself
Auditing benchmark calculator formulas against current clinical guidelines (16 of 55 flagged for version, use or coefficient concerns)

screen.practice: deterministic code executor for LLM clinical calculations
screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluating whether handing arithmetic off to a deterministic Python executor/solver safeguards against LLM calculation errors in clinical calculator tasks compared to direct LLM generation.
